rationale: Fold the grow/shrink control into the phantom-configuration account: the phantom configuration appears in both directions, but the commit without a real quorum occurred only after a failed removal, while the failed addition still committed with the other voter's acknowledgement. The limitation now states the two directions exercised instead of a single configuration shape.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A configuration change whose log write fails is reported to the caller as failed, but the new configuration is nevertheless installed in the leader's in-memory latest configuration at the index the entry would have occupied. The node then treats that unstored configuration as authoritative: it re-elects itself with the shrunken voter set and reports a client command committed with only its own acknowledgement, while the other member of the committed configuration does not have that entry. Evidence from receipt 0e6dd623c01e43a4b9e33cafc544ecf2 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0). Parsed index 0, the case event: two voters were bootstrapped, the leader's store failed exactly the configuration write, and afterwards latest_index_after_fail=3 with last_log_index_after_fail=2, while phantom_servers records the shrunken configuration containing only the leader itself. Parsed index 1, the result: remove_failed=true with remove_error 'injected store failure', latest_index_exceeds_log=true, re_elected=true, apply_ok=true, commit_index=4, leader_last_index=4 and peer_last_index=2, so commit_without_peer=true. Under the committed two-voter configuration a quorum is both members, so the command the client was told had committed at index 4 never reached a quorum of that configuration. Mechanism from source: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, unconditionally, calls setLatestConfiguration with the new configuration at the dispatched index, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication (raft.go:1204-1244), while dispatchLogs' store-error path only answers the futures with the error and moves the node to follower (raft.go:1245-1296). quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all read that latest configuration (raft.go:1087-1100, 1999-2071, 456-468), so the phantom configuration governs both the election the node wins alone and the quorum it uses to commit. Consequence under the exercised conditions: after a transient failure to store a configuration change, the leader can adopt a voter set that the rest of the cluster never accepted and serve client commits that no quorum of the committed configuration holds. The restart phase of successor receipt 76bdaf3e107643d4a3ed1247faa52460 is withdrawn as evidence: that harness created a fresh in-memory transport for the restarted node without connecting it to the other member's transport, so the restarted node could not reach the peer at all. Its restarted_as_leader=false and the peer's unchanged log index are therefore explained by the missing transport wiring, not by the target's recovery behaviour, and nothing is concluded from that phase beyond the fact that the log store still held the commit when the node was rebuilt (lone_commit_retained=true, which reads only the store). Recovery after restart remains unmeasured. The target's own membership document states the condition this violates: a new configuration 'will be in affect as soon as it is appended to the log' (membership.md:15). In the failed-write case nothing was appended, so the condition the document sets for a configuration to take effect was never met, yet the node used the new voter set for its election and for committing. A boundary control, receipt 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d, repeats the failed write in both directions: after a failed RemoveServer the phantom configuration contains only the leader and the later command commits with commit_without_peer=true (parsed index 1), while after a failed AddVoter the phantom configuration names the two real voters plus an unreachable third and the same command commits with commit_without_peer=false, the other real voter holding index 4 (parsed index 4). The phantom configuration therefore forms in both directions, but the missing-quorum commit occurs only when the failed change would have shrunk the voter set, because a grown phantom quorum still requires a majority of the committed voters.

knowledge.assertion: appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration in memory regardless of whether its log entry was stored.
quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState derive voter sets from the latest configuration.

counterevidence: The phantom state does not outlive a restart: in receipt adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 the restarted node led again and the peer's log reached the same index, so the entry first committed alone later became a quorum commit of the committed configuration. The durability hazard is therefore confined to the interval between that lone commit and a successful restart with the peer reachable.

The commit without a peer required the store to fail once and then succeed: the harness fails a single StoreLogs call, and a persistent write failure would also block the later client command, so the exercised trigger is a transient store error rather than a permanent one.

The other voter never accepted the phantom configuration and still holds the committed two-voter view, so its own elections fail while the phantom leader lives; the harness observed the leader's side only and did not measure how long the peer stays unable to win.
No data was corrupted: the client command was applied to the phantom leader's own state machine, and the failure mode is a commit reported without a quorum of the committed configuration.

The consequence is bounded to failed changes that would remove a voter: in the grow-direction control (receipt 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d, parsed index 4) the command committed after the failed AddVoter and the other real voter held the same index, so a grown phantom configuration did not produce an unsupported commit.
limitations: Two configuration directions were exercised (removing the only other voter and adding an unreachable third), each once; no repetition, no three-member committed configuration and no non-voter in the committed configuration.
The harness applies its command immediately after the node returns to Leader and does not test whether a later successful configuration change repairs or compounds the phantom view.

Recovery was measured in one configuration only: the restart led again and the peer caught up, with the peer reachable throughout. The case where the node never restarts, or restarts while the peer is unreachable, is the interval in which the lone commit stays unsupported and was not exercised.
The client-visible completion point was the Apply future returning nil; no read path through the FSM was exercised.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt adbbb5d29a08477b9dbbd7da187f7f26 is the third revision of 6491640ed49a4c7b8f5150438d350e36-experiment under this question and replaces the restart phase of the second revision, whose transport wiring was defective. The failed change, the phantom configuration and the lone commit are identical across the first and third receipts, so the events describe the same subject; the third adds a valid restart observation. Receipt 99292afefb9d4308957a0e2d150bf11d is the fourth revision of the same experiment and adds the grow-direction control; its shrink case reproduces the earlier receipt's outcome, and its grow case supplies the boundary that the earlier revisions lacked.
